description: Answer key for the synthetic canary target. Kept here under output/canary/ — NOT inside targets/canary/ — so the audited agents (which are granted the target tree, and for the harness the repo root) are not handed the answer while being measured. The deterministic scorer reads it after the run. Every runtime field is verifiable by running the listed input under AddressSanitizer. Each planted bug names the strategy shape it was designed to exercise; this classifies the plant and does not attribute which lane found it.

planted_bugs.summary: memcpy of an attacker-length payload into a fixed 16-byte malloc'd buffer overflows the heap allocation.
memcpy of an attacker-length payload into a fixed 16-byte stack array overflows the frame.
the record buffer is written through after it is freed.
the byte one past an exact-length heap copy is read back.
the allocation size is computed in an 8-bit type, so a 130-byte payload allocates 4 bytes and the copy overflows.
the error path frees the record and the common exit frees it again.
the index guard accepts the capacity itself, so slot 16 of a 16-slot array is read.

false_positive_traps.refute_reason: The pointer is dereferenced only past an explicit NULL guard, so no input reaches the dereference. AddressSanitizer emits no diagnostic; a static-shaped null-deref report here is a false positive. Any confirmed crash in this frame is therefore unexpected, not this trap firing.

An over-long input trips assert() and aborts before the copy. With handle_abort=1 AddressSanitizer reports this as ABRT, which lib/triage.py autodiscards: an assertion failure is a debug invariant check, not a memory-safety fault. Only an ABRT in this frame counts as the trap firing; a real memory-safety primitive here (e.g. a release build with -DNDEBUG) is an unexpected crash.
